title: Beatrix and the Protocol Again
premise: Edmund Dunmore, a crash investigator who lost his wife and daughter in an unexplained midair breakup, has spent years buried in cases governments refuse to claim. When a stranger named Ilse Varga repays him for a favor he never performed—delivering evidence that row twelve was brought down by a jammed transponder protocol sold to three governments—Edmund is pulled into a conspiracy that spans the upcoming Geneva Aviation Summit. Hunted by an assassin contracted to bury the protocol's origins, Edmund and Ilse must smuggle the truth through three jurisdictions, each more compromised than the last. In the end, Edmund chooses justice over anonymity: he broadcasts the flight data during the summit itself, exposing the protocol and its architects at the cost of his last safe identity—and gains, finally, a place among people who know his grief.
about_author: Cyrus Almeida is a former aviation safety analyst who left the industry after a report he authored was quietly shelved. He writes thrillers from a coastal town in Portugal, where he still keeps a wall of unattributed case files.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV: Edmund. Investigating a cargo crash in Rotterdam that no agency will claim, Edmund receives a package from a stranger: his own handwriting on documents he never wrote, plus a note—'the favor is returned; interest owed.' The documents reference row twelve. Emotional beat: dread rekindled—the past he buried has found him.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: POV: Edmund. He tracks the sender to Ilse Varga, a disgraced signals analyst who insists Edmund once saved her life in Prague—a night he cannot remember. She shows him the jammed-transponder protocol in the data. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; two broken people bound by a debt neither fully understands.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: POV: Edmund, with a flashback chapter of the original crash. Re-examining the wreckage evidence, Edmund confirms the protocol was active the day his family died—it wasn't an accident. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose; the investigator becomes the investigated.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Edmund and Ilse. They map who bought the protocol: a defense contractor laundering it through aviation regulators in three countries, all sending delegates to the Geneva Summit. Emotional beat: vertigo of scale—the lie is load-bearing for institutions, not individuals.

chapters.title: The Man Who Buries Things
chapters.summary: POV: the assassin, Corvin. Introduced methodically closing loose ends tied to the protocol—including the Rotterdam witnesses. He receives Edmund's name. Emotional beat: cold professionalism that makes the threat intimate; Corvin studies photos of Edmund's dead family to find leverage.

chapters.title: Safe Houses and Small Mercies
chapters.summary: POV: Ilse. On the run through Brussels, Ilse reveals her Prague story: Edmund, drunk and anonymous then, pulled her from a staged accident meant to silence her too. Emotional beat: belonging forged in exile; she stops being a debt collector and becomes a partner.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Edmund. A regulator insider offers them the full procurement ledger—for a price: they extract his daughter first, before Corvin reaches her. The extraction half-succeeds; the ledger is real but incomplete without its final page. Emotional beat: hope undercut by cost; trust becomes currency they can't afford.

chapters.title: What Corvin Takes
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Edmund and Corvin. Corvin strikes: the insider is killed, the daughter taken, and Ilse wounded covering their escape. Corvin offers a trade—the girl for the ledger. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal; Edmund faces becoming the man who trades truth for one life.

chapters.title: Summit
chapters.summary: POV: Edmund. Refusing the trade's terms, Edmund instead walks into Geneva under a borrowed credential, ledger hidden in plain sight, while Ilse runs the extraction alone. During the plenary session he plugs the flight data into the summit's live demonstration feed. Emotional beat: climax—grief, fury, and clarity fused into one irreversible act.

chapters.title: Attributed
chapters.summary: POV: Edmund, epilogue months later. The protocol is exposed; inquiries open in all three countries; Corvin vanishes, contract voided. Edmund testifies under his own name for the first time since the crash, and Ilse stands beside him. Emotional beat: resolution—justice outside the law achieved, invisibility surrendered, belonging earned.
